summary: GitHub Pages serves from gh-pages while new files land on master; scheduled workflows that only update a narrow path (e.g., api/ecosystem.json) can leave gh-pages stale, causing persistent Pages 404s for master-only files.

evidence.root_cause: gh-pages branch did not contain newly-added HTML files present on master; scheduled workflow updated only api/ecosystem.json on gh-pages.

recommended_diagnosis: Check GitHub Pages publishing source branch (often gh-pages).
Probe raw gh-pages for the missing file; if it is absent there but present on master, the issue is branch drift.
Inspect scheduled workflows for partial-tree updates to gh-pages.
recommended_mitigation: In any workflow that commits to gh-pages, sync the full tree from master into gh-pages before applying generated updates.
Use 'git add -A' so deletions and new files are staged.
Prefer invariant checks that compare master vs gh-pages for expected published files.
